bothSidesReview.eligibility: On-record named-org opposition (Brennan Center analyses) plus a closely-split recorded floor vote on the policy (S. 1383 House amendment, 218-213). Not false balance.
bothSidesReview.verbSymmetry: pass — only argue/argues/says/said/contends/adds/cites used across both sides; none of notes/points out/claims/alleges/acknowledges/admits. Enforced by scripts/tracker-gate.js.
bothSidesReview.stripTest: pass — every argumentative sentence names its holder (Brennan Center / Cornyn / Roy & Lee) and resolves to a stored source; unattributed/unsourced assertions were removed (see fixed rows). Confirmed by the cross-model verifier and both lens reviewers.
bothSidesReview.vehicleBill: HUMAN-verified 2026-08-19 (Opus, in-conversation): the policy's decisive floor vote rode S. 1383 (218-213, Roll 69, 2026-02-11); S. 1383 latest action "Considered by Senate" (2026-03-26), still pending, not enacted. The tracked number (H.R. 7296) has no floor action of its own. The panel approve step re-surfaces this as a blocking human checkbox.
bothSidesReview.staleness: pass (scripts/tracker-gate.js staleness check + npm run stale)

supporterLens.note: Supporter-lens reviewer signed off after two passes: security rationale, federal-preemption rationale, and Texas precedent all present and verbatim-accurate; tone symmetry restored by quoting the sponsors' own charged term.

resolution: Retrofit of a pre-lane both-sides tracker (published 2026-07-17 with linked-not-stored sources and no ledger). Every named position fetched and STORED (11 primary sources: 2 bill texts, 3 Congress.gov records, 1 House roll-call record, 5 org/member statements). 11 findings fixed: 2 material omissions (unsourced 80% popularity claim; unsourced attestation-baseline contrast) removed per Sec 6.4; 9 minor. The both-sides section was expanded on the dual-lens QC to fairly and fully represent both sides (federal-preemption + Texas precedent added on the supporter side; failsafe/criminal-penalty + DHS data-sharing + Arizona/Kansas precedent added on the opponent side), with the sponsors' charged term quoted verbatim for tone symmetry.
